id: title:Gilbert09:treat jsonb path deletion on a scalar as non retryable

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a permanent, non-retryable classification for Postgres warehouse ingestion errors, preventing repeated ingestion attempts on deterministic failures.
review.reason: The change adds a specific, permanent error classification ('cannot delete path in scalar') for Postgres warehouse ingestion failures and includes a corresponding regression test. This represents a substantive improvement in warehouse ingestion reliability by distinguishing deterministic failures from transient ones, preventing unnecessary retry loops. review.uncertainty: The benefit relies on the assumption that this specific error is deterministic and not transient; while the classification is permanent, the underlying cause is not independently verified. No adoption or incident avoidance is inferred.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned. No adoption, incident, or benefit inferred. No tier assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a non-retryable error entry and a corresponding test.
observations.code_quote: "cannot delete path in scalar": "A view you're syncing deletes a key or path from a JSON value with the #- operator (or jsonb_delete_path()), and that value is a scalar for at least one row, so Postgres can't evaluate the view and we can't read it. Guard the call in your view definition (for example only delete the path when jsonb_typeof(col) is 'object' or 'array'), or remove that view from the sync.",
